name: late-run-error-after-finished-fails-the-run
description: RUN_ERROR after RUN_FINISHED is admitted — a failure that surfaced after the run reported success — everything delivered before the failure is kept, and the consumer treats the run as failed rather than reporting the RUN_FINISHED result as a success
kill: remove the RUN_ERROR exemption from the `runFinished` guard in verifyEvents — the late failure then fails with `The run has already finished with 'RUN_FINISHED'` instead of the producer's own message, and `errorContains` fails. Removing the failure from the RUN_ERROR case in the reducer kills it the other way, leaving the run completed with its success result

stream.message: late-run-error: the transport failed while flushing

expect.errorContains: late-run-error: the transport failed while flushing
expect.runError: late-run-error: the transport failed while flushing

dotnet.intentional: The .NET client has no reducer stage that can fail a run: EventStreamConverter reports RUN_ERROR as an ErrorContent update and the enumeration completes, so the stream is consumed successfully and the failure is observable only through `runError` (asserted above, unchanged). `errorContains` is deliberately the empty string, which asserts nothing — it LIFTS the base's requirement rather than restating it, because this lane produces no rejection to match against. Closing this divergence means giving the .NET client a way to surface a reported run failure as a failed consumption, and deleting this override.
